Q: <c:url value="/faq#1" var="faqLink"> How to preserve # in exported variable which is mandatory and wrap functionality into tag? A:

सावन का महीना शुरू होते ही गाँव में हर तरफ हरियाली छा गई। सुबह-सुबह मंदिर की घंटियाँ बजने लगीं और भक्त भगवान शिव को जल चढ़ाने जाने लगे। गाँव का छोटा बच्चा मोहन भी अपनी माँ के साथ शिव मंदिर पहुँचा। उसने शिवलिंग पर जल और बेलपत्र चढ़ाकर प्रार्थना की, “भोलेनाथ, हमारे गाँव में हमेशा सुख-शांति बनाए रखना।”

अचानक मंदिर के बाहर तेज बारिश शुरू हो गई। मोहन मुस्कुराते हुए बोला, “माँ, लगता है भोलेनाथ ने हमारी प्रार्थना सुन ली!”

माँ ने कहा, “बेटा, सच्ची श्रद्धा और अच्छे कर्म ही सबसे बड़ी पूजा हैं।”

उस दिन से मोहन हर सावन में जरूरतमंदों की मदद करने लगा।

Q: CSS for display with flex across multiple browsers? A:

It looks like Chrome is applying a different layout than Firefox. recommend using Chrome DevTools (F12) to inspect the .menu element and check whether another CSS rule is overriding display: flex or flex-wrap. Also try temporarily removing the older vendor-prefixed display declarations and keep only display: flex with flex-wrap: nowrap. If the problem remains, a minimal reproducible example (or the live page) would make it much easier to identify the exact rule causing the menu items to stack vertically.

Q: prism::get_prism_dailys() fails with “SSL connect error” when downloading PRISM data A:

The status check works fine (that's httr) but the actual download.file() call fails because that's a mismatch which usually means different TLS/HTTP clients are being used under the hood. On Windows, download.file() defaults to wininet, which sometimes struggles with SSL negotiation even when other tools connect fine. Try switching methods:

options(download.file.method = "libcurl")

Also test the URL directly, outside the package:

download.file("https://services.nacse.org/prism/data/get/us/800m/ppt/20250601?format=bil", "test.zip", mode="wb")

If it's still a issue, it might be due to proxy/firewall doing SSL inspection, or outdated OpenSSL. I would suggest try updating R, or use curl::curl_download() instead.

Q: So where should I keep .env files? A:

After reading this, that, this, and other articles, I concluded that there is no certain answer for this question; it depends on your organization / your preferences.

The recommended method for most applications is to save them at the root of your project, but include them in your .gitignore file in order to avoid them from being committed to your main repo (one .env file corresponds to each device/environment).

Other methods suggest including them in your repo, but encrypting and decrypting all the passwords inside of them once they load. Another method is to store them in password management programs like KeyPass, It really depends on how much effort you want to invest in the security and the time you would like to spend maintaining your application.

Q: Query with LIKE / IN A:

You could convert the comma separated parameter/list to a JSON array and using JSON_TABLE . (I took it for granted that Oracle is used from the MATCH_RECOGNIZE (even if it is supported by other RDBMS) and JSON_TABLE is supported as well).

SELECT DISTINCT a.*
FROM article a
JOIN JSON_TABLE(
       '["' || REPLACE('AAPL,IBM,DELL,UNP', ',', '","') || '"]',
       '$[*]' COLUMNS (
           ticker VARCHAR2(20) PATH '$'
       )
     ) p
  ON INSTR(',' || a.tickers || ',', ',' || p.ticker || ',') > 0;

JSON_TABLE() converts the JSON array into rows, the JSON array is created by the '["' || REPLACE('AAPL,IBM,DELL,UNP', ',', '","') || '"]' which would give ["AAPL","IBM","DELL","UNP"]. INSTR() is used for the exact match

'AAPL,IBM,DELL,UNP' is the list/parameter See example

The real issue is the table design. Storing a delimited list has a lot off disadvantages, see Is storing a delimited list in a database column really that bad? for further details. Fix the schema if possible.

Q: Export Git with version history A:

You want to create a fork of your current repository it would seem.

Let me know if I got this right: You wish to clone a particular Git repository. Work on the clone and then merge the changes into the original repository?

This is done by creating a fork of your repository and then pulling the changes from the original source for commit changes.

Q: Is SQL Server Express' 4GB limit affected by FILESTREAM enabled columns? A:

According to Mike Wachal (a program manager in the SQL Server group) in this forum post (archive), the pointer information to the blobs is included, but the blobs themselves are not:

A quick note on the 4 GB limit: This is applied per database and includes all the user data included the primary (mdf) and secondary (ndf) data files. Log files (ldf) are not included in this count. The behavior is that your database will be read-only when the limit is reached and will error if you try to insert additional data. As pointed out by Papy, there is a new feature in SQL 2008 called Filestream that allows for the storage of BLOB data directly on disk with a pointer to it stored in the database. The on disk BLOB does not count toward the 4 GB limit but the pointer information does (although it is much smaller).

I know it's not "official documentation", but it does come from someone within the SQL Server group.

Q: Compress(minimize) HTML from python A:

For anyone who's interested.

htmlmin hasn't been maintained for years (the latest stable version is from 2017), and some internal dependencies have caused compatibility issues with modern versions of Python starting with 3.13

There is a fork of htmlmin created specifically to maintain compatibility: htmlmin4

pip install htmlmin4

Its usage is identical; as you can see, no changes are required.

from htmlmin import minify

html_min = minify(
html,
remove_comments=True,
remove_empty_space=True
)
